check2_followup: Inside the spec, 10 of the 12 check-2 findings are fixed: precheck G13 deferral and outcome mapping; G02, G04, G05 and G14 owned here, with the screening-age row in table 1a; verdict shaping; effector registration and the holder-cap maximum; the twelve Unlocks; halt backend hand-over and duplicate names; the G22 mismatch, reservation and CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED mapping; agent audit fields; s761G citations. Two are not fully fixed. The G13 binding now works inside A19, but its fixed single-line payload shape conflicts with A38 and A39 (finding 2). The graph summaries in app-graph.json and final-graph.json are still stale (finding 10). The lock-up fix added a new conflict with A18 (finding 3), and the tipping-off fix contradicts itself (finding 6).

findings.issue: G07 double-counts at mint. A18 and A38 are register-first: the trustee's issue entry is acked before A28 mints. So when assertPassed(requireFresh) re-runs the mint row inside the mint transaction, holdings already include the allocated units, and the formula units_after = holdings + open_order_units + requested adds them a second time. total_units ('units on issue after the action') is counted twice the same way. Example: an allocation of 500 on a 10,000-unit vehicle passes at precheck and at allocation, then fails G07 at mint (1,000 > 500). That stalls the whole batch mint.
findings.fix: Define G07 per kind. For mint: units_after = register holdings as of the acked issue (requested counted only if the issue entry is not yet on the register, identified by the approval_id), and total_units = units on issue per A18, never re-added. Add an oracle vector: a 500-of-10,000 allocation passes G07 at order, allocation and mint with the register entry already acked.

findings.issue: approvalPayloadFor's single-line shape conflicts with the upstream approval payloads, so G13 cannot pass for real mints and withdrawals. A38's allocation.mint approval is one request per locked Allocation file (object_ref = allocation_id, payload_sha256 = allocation_sha256, many lines). A39's withdrawal.release payload_sha256 is the withdrawal row's canonical hash, which binds the destination. G13 requires payload_sha256 = sha256(approvalPayloadFor(code, ctx)) over one investor, one quantity and no destination or wallet. Specify item 12 then forces A38 and A39 to switch to that shape. That breaks batch minting and drops the destination account and the recipient wallet from the approval binding. Neither action_sha256 nor approvalPayloadFor contains ctx.wallet or a destination. Oracle vector (k) encodes the single-line model.
findings.fix: Make the payload binding per action code. Add registerApprovalPayload(action_code, {canonical(ctx) -> string, lineIn(ctx, payload) -> bool}), owned by the drafting module: A38 registers the file shape (ctx carries batch_ref {allocation_id, version, sha256} and G13 also checks that the line (investor, units, wallet) is in the locked file); A39 registers its row canonical, including destination. Add wallet and destination_ref to action_sha256. Drop A38 and A39 from Specify item 12. Rewrite vector (k) as a line that is not in the approved file (fails G13_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH) and a changed destination (fails).

findings.issue: The lock-up effector contradicts A18's frozen path. A18 says lock-up changes reach the register only through adjust/lot_attribute, called by A28, chain first, under action codes token.lock_up / token.unlock at 4E+Q, applied after broadcast or confirmed. A19's rules.lockup.set effector writes lot dates register-first through 'A18's instruction path' with no custody step, emits an event for A28 afterwards, and puts a trigger on register_lot.lock_in_until, a table A18 owns. A18 will refuse the write, or the build will bypass A18's path, and in the meantime the register and the chain diverge.
findings.fix: Remove rules.lockup.set as an A19 effector and remove register_lot.lock_in_until from A19's trigger list. PUT vehicles/{id}/lockups validates (G08 and the simulator) and drafts A28's token.lock_up request (REGO maker, CCO checker, 4E+Q, one approval id). A28 executes chain first, then A18 lot_attribute. Update oracle (o) and the ADM-16 'Set lock-up dates' text to match.

findings.issue: The compliance-rule change skips the chain. The product map marks ADM-16 'Change rule parameter' as on-chain, and A28 already has the op rule_change (compliance-module parameter call, CCO to LEGL, 4E+Q, simulation attached from A19). A19 defines its own rules.compliance_rule.change (4E, no custody), whose effector makes the off-chain params effective at once and emits nothing for A28. Result: two approvals for one change, which breaks the one-approval-id rule, and the on-chain module keeps the old parameters. A20 R6 then raises Sev1 rule_drift and halts the vehicle after every approved cap change.
findings.fix: Use one 4E+Q approval (A28's rule_change code, or rename A19's code and make A28 consume it). Sequence it: the approval executes A28's on-chain call first; on confirmed, A19's effector sets the compliance_rule effective with the same approval_id and params_sha256 (or emits rules.compliance_rule.changed for A28 under that id, with A20 R6 treating the in-flight approval as pending, not drift). Add a vector: after an approved cap change, R6 reports no drift.

findings.issue: G13 can be bypassed for 4E withdrawals because applicability is decided by the wrong source. Table 3 accepts G13 not_applicable on a withdrawal 'below withdrawal.second_approval_cents' (A$50k). A14 and A16 require an approval for every withdrawal: AUTO up to A$25k allow-listed, 4E above A$25k or to a non-allow-listed destination or over the same-day sum, 6E from A$50k. A16 says no copy or config key of these tiers may exist, yet table 1a keeps withdrawal.second_approval_cents. So a A$30k withdrawal (4E, CFO checker) passes G13 as not_applicable. More generally, 'G13 when no policy code' (transfer, announcement) and the offer_submit condition rest on the caller-supplied ctx.policy_code; a caller that omits it gets not_applicable.
findings.fix: Delete withdrawal.second_approval_cents from table 1a. Add a fact approval_policy from A14's resolver (the policy row for the action code and the frozen amounts) and decide G13 applicability from it, never from ctx.policy_code presence. For withdrawal, G13 is never valid not_applicable (AUTO requests are checked too). Add vectors: a A$30k withdrawal with no approval fails G13_APPROVAL_MISSING, and a context with policy_code omitted still resolves the policy.

findings.issue: The tipping-off rule contradicts itself, so pass criterion (n) cannot be met as written. The shaping replaces only a non-pass G02 or G14 and shows a passing G02 or G14 as it is. For an investor under a G14 restriction with clear screening, the order set therefore shows G02 as pass ('No matches') and G14 as UNDER_REVIEW. For an investor whose screening is in review, it shows G02 as UNDER_REVIEW and G14 as pass. The two responses differ, yet the spec requires them to be byte-identical. The spec also does not say whether the neutral verdict keeps gate G02 (rendered 'Sanctions and PEP (G02)'), which would itself tell the investor that a sanctions review is open.
findings.fix: For the subject, their agents and tenant principals, when either G02 or G14 is non-pass, remove both rows and emit one neutral verdict with gate 'ACCOUNT_REVIEW', hold, UNDER_REVIEW and fix-it gate.under_review, in a fixed position. When both pass, show both as they are. State that the gate id G02 or G14 never appears on a shaped non-pass. Oracle (n) then compares these two cases plus 'both non-pass'.

findings.issue: G13's expiry rule contradicts A14's two clocks. G13 fails G13_EXPIRED when now is past expires_at or execution_deadline in any accepted state. A14 closes the decision TTL once a timelocked request reaches queued, and applies neither clock after custody has a signature. So a timelocked 6E op approved at hour 71 with a 48 h timelock, which A14's own oracle says must still execute, fails G13 at requireFresh in queued_for_custody. G13 also omits queued (timelock not elapsed) and lists 'vetoed', which is not an A14 state (a veto goes to cancelled).
findings.fix: Apply A14's clocks by state: approved (no timelock) checks expires_at; queued_for_custody checks execution_deadline; signed and broadcast check neither; queued gives hold G13_TIMELOCK_PENDING. Better still, call an A14-exported isExecutable(approvalId, now). Replace 'vetoed' with cancelled. Add A14's hour-71 timelock vector.

findings.issue: A future-dated pack can never become effective. The rules.pack.change effector moves a pack to approved_pending_effect when effective_from is in the future. The later switch to effective needs a writer, but no job is named, and the section-1 trigger refuses state = effective unless the transaction carries an approval that is approved or executing under that effector. By then A14 has taken the request to confirmed, reconciled or closed. The pack stays pending for ever, and rules.pack.published never fires.
findings.fix: Name a worker job, rules.packs.activate (every minute, idempotent), under the owned worker path. It switches approved_pending_effect to effective when effective_from <= now, supersedes the old pack in the same transaction and emits rules.pack.published. Let the trigger accept that single transition when the row's approval_id request has completed for rules.pack.change. Add a vector: a pack approved for effective_from = now + 1 day is effective one day later, and the old pack is superseded.

findings.issue: The member-count monitor would breach on almost every real vehicle. It breaches when distinct members exceed 20 (s601ED(1)(a)) and emits alerts. Wholesale schemes rely on the s601ED(2) exemption, and the product map's ADM-16 monitor table shows vehicles with 188, 412 and 903 members in 'ok' state. As specified, every real vehicle would sit in 'breached' with standing Sev alerts, and the ADM-16 rendering would not match the product map.
findings.fix: Add a per-vehicle compliance_rule.s601ED_basis ('exempt_s601ED2' | 'must_register_above_20', counsel_pending). For exempt wholesale vehicles the metric is informational, with no warning or breach. It warns or breaches only for vehicles not recorded as exempt. Keep the counsel question.

findings.issue: The graph summaries are still stale. app-graph.json and final-graph.json still say 'a 500-token order failing G07', 'G05/G09/G15 return not applicable', 'G22 registered from the agent-authority package' and 's601ED (default 20)'. final-graph.json still has deps [A09, A03, A12], est 10-14 and one owned path. graph-revisions.json lists the summary change as 'not applied'. The spec now says the note wins and that Fable writes the oracle from the note only, but the orchestrator still hands the stale summary to the builder and to Fable as node data.
findings.fix: Before the A19 run, apply the summary text of Specify item 1 to both graph files, add A14, A18 and A21 to final-graph.json's deps, align est 12-16 and both owned paths, and regenerate. Remove the item from graph-revisions open_items.

findings.issue: The masking of G14 also hides a fix the investor can make. A withdrawal refused because withdrawal_destination.in_name_verified is false is a non-pass G14, so it is shaped to UNDER_REVIEW with no fix-it, even though it is not AML-sensitive and the investor has to correct their bank account. The failure also has no named reason code.
findings.fix: Give the check its own code, G14_DESTINATION_NOT_IN_NAME (or move it to a separate withdrawal check), exempt it from shaping, and give it the fix-it 'Use an account in your own name'. Add a vector.
